newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cricket - Bat first in 2nd test, groundsman warns.
newsitem.headline: Cricket - Bat first in 2nd test, groundsman warns.

text.p: HAMILTON, March 13 - Not even New Zealand newcomer Andrew Penn is expected to be as nervous as Hamilton groundsman Ian McKendry heading into the second cricket test against Sri Lanka starting on Friday, NZPA reports.
The pitch has attracted a lot of attention this summer following some extraordinary results at Trust Bank Park, threatening to turn the test into a benefit match for the seam bowlers.
Northern Districts seamer Alex Tait returned the best figures in New Zealand first-class cricket history when claiming a match analysis of 16 for 130 against Auckland last month.
The same game saw Northern dismissed for 32, the second lowest score at first-class level in this country this century.

McKendry, who assisted Lancaster Park groundsman Russell Wyllie in Christchurch for nine years before shifting to Hamilton last winter, has been working 60-hour weeks for the past month to present a sound playing surface for the test, but his preparation has been hampered by 70mm of rain since March 1.

Northern Districts officials have decided the wicket block will be dug up and relaid this winter, but that is of no help to McKendry, who faces a stiff ask to present a surface agreeable to the two test teams.

Tait has benefited greatly from the liberal seam movement provided by the pitch, capturing 27 wickets in just three games here this season, but he does not hold McKendry accountable for the pitch's behaviour.
"The Northern Districts boys have some sympathy for the groundsman because the track was left in a bad condition at the end of last season.
"He's been asked to make a silk purse out of a sow's ear this year," Tait said.
McKendry is quietly confident his labours will ensure the pitch is up to standard for a test match, but he has no hesitation in suggesting the captain winning the toss should bat first.
"As with any pitch there has to be uncertainty whether it'll last five days, and if I was a captain I'd definitely bat first. I wouldn't want to bat last on it," he said.
New Zealand coach Steve Rixon made a brief inspection of the pitch yesterday, and came away saying it looked different to that on which England played Northern Districts here in late January.
"It was quite enlightening having a look at it. It's now quite dry.
"It looks like a good wicket, it's flat and it'll carry but I don't think it will have as much sideways movement as we originally thought."
Rixon raised the prospect of newcomer Penn opening the attack with Simon Doull irrespective of whether Heath Davis is fit enough to play.

Davis was to have a fitness test this afternoon on Achilles tendon and knee injuries which dogged him in the first test in Dunedin earlier this week when New Zealand stormed their way to victory by an innings and 36 runs.

The humidity in Hamilton at this time of the year normally suits bowlers who have the ability to move the ball in the air, which is one of Doull's trademarks and a strength of Central Districts 22-year-old Penn.
"Penn could open. He's a genuine swinger of the ball whereas Heath is not. It is certainly an option," Rixon said.
Wellington medium pacer Gavin Larsen is on standby to be considered for selection should Davis be ruled out for the game.

Sri Lanka, who performed well below expectations in Dunedin where several factors -- lack of tour matches, cold weather and some questionable umpiring decisions -- conspired against them, need to lift their game significantly to be competitive here.
Their bowling was inaccurate, their batsmen too prone to flash strokes and their fielding sloppy in Dunedin.
"We know what went wrong in Dunedin and we want to do the right things in Hamilton," captain Arjuna Ranatunga said.
"We have to sort out the batting, bowling and fielding."
Sri Lanka were to inspect the match venue today but it is difficult seeing the tourists making any changes to their lineup.

New Zealand: Stephen Fleming (captain), Blair Pocock, Bryan Young, Matt Horne, Nathan Astle, Chris Cairns, Adam Parore, Dipak Patel, Daniel Vettori, Simon Doull, Heath Davis, Andrew Penn and Gavin Larsen. (two to be omitted).

Sri Lanka: Arjuna Ranatunga (captain), Sanath Jayasuriya, Roshan Mahanama, Marvan Atapattu, Aravinda de Silva, Hashan Tillekaratne, Romesh Kaluwitharana, Chaminda Vaas, Pramodya Wickremasinghe, Nuwan Zoysa, Muttiah Muralitharan, Dulip Samaraweera, Kumar Dharmasena, Sajeewa de Silva and Ravindra Pushpakumara. (four to be omitted).
